pageCache.pageTitle: St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School – Our Lady of Grace Catholic Academy Trust
pageCache.text:
HeadTeacher’s Message
Welcome and thank you for taking the time to visit the St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School website.
St Winefride’s is a friendly, happy, family-like environment where children can flourish spiritually, socially and academically.
We are committed to our vision of ensuring every child at St Winefride’s is equal, supported and celebrated as we aim to develop confident and responsible individuals who aspire to reach their full potential.
Our curriculum offer is based on teaching the children about the challenges the world is facing, having the inspiration to improve and preserve the future of our planet, and to live happy and kind lives in the way that Jesus teaches us.
We recognise and value the partnership between school, home and church and are committed to living out our mission statement and ensuring it is at the heart of all we do:
We celebrate God’s love for everyone.
We enjoy learning and growing together in our caring and welcoming family.
I hope this website provides you with all the information you require about our school. Please click the video below to see a glimpse of life at St Winefride’s.
Please feel free to contact us for more information.
Mrs Brosnan Head Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education Curriculum – St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
At St Winefride’s we follow the ‘Come and See’ programme for Foundation and Key Stages 1 and 2, which is endorsed by the Diocese of Brentwood. 10% of the teaching timetable is provided for Religious Education. This means, 2 hours 15 minutes at Foundation Stage and Key Stage 1, and 2 hours 30 minutes at Key Stage 2. This time does not include collective worship (other than the Rejoice section), hymn practice, assemblies etc. This time allocation is distributed appropriately across the timetable to ensure quality time is given for effective teaching and learning throughout the week. Allocation of teaching time to other faiths is 5 hours (2 weeks RE time). The school leadership and management take responsibility for this.
Within each lesson there is a balance between input, discussion and activity.
The Catechism of the Catholic Church addresses the human search for meaning, God’s initiative in Revelation who comes to meet us and our response of faith. This pattern guides the structure of the programme and informs the process of each topic, opened up through; Explore, Reveal and Respond.
The teacher helps the children to begin to look at and focus on the experience within their own lives – concerning themselves, their relationships and their world. In this way the children are led to a deeper understanding, clearer vision and the discovery of significance and value of the experiential events of everyday life.
Reveal is the heart of the process. The teacher and the children together discover the Christian understanding of the mystery of the Trinity; Father, Son and Holy Spirit. They explore the mystery of human life as revealed in the person, life and gospel of Jesus Christ. It will involve learning about Scripture, the teaching of the Church, prayers, rites, psalms, hymns and other expressions of Christian faith and the lives of outstanding Christians
‘Remember’ is the first part of this section. The children will respond by remembering and celebrating all that they have learnt. This new understanding will enable them to make a personal response in their daily lives. This part begins by reflecting on what the children wonder about. This is followed by providing the opportunity for the children to remember what they have understood and learnt.
For an overview of the RE Curriculum please click the link below:
Overview of the RE curriculum
Click here to see our full Religious Education Site.
Other ways we spread the good news of Jesus throughout the school.
Every class has their own prayer table, which the children help to keep clean and tidy, the cloths covering the tables are changed to reflect the time of the church year.
The Gospel is central to our lives at St Winefride’s and the scripture is displayed every week along with a prayer for the children to read. This prayer is included in the newsletter every week.
Our yearly Cafod fundraising events during Lent are one of the highlights of the school year.
Our Mini Vinnies carry out lots of good work for both charity and the school. They have made, packaged and sold cookies, run stalls and organise the ‘Reverse Advent calendar’, they are a marvellous asset for the school.
The RE Team plays a vital role in the school, monitoring classroom setups, talking to the children and helping to teach them class prayers, helping to set the Intention of the Week and setting a good example by raising the Catholic profile of the school.
All pupils are at the centre of shaping the school’s ethos. Pupil Responsibilities and participation in the Catholic life of the school are of an exceptionally high standard. For example the children take pride in singing their mission statement daily and applying it to everyday life. All staff and governors are committed to living the Gospel Values to be outstanding role models to the pupils.
All pupils, regardless of starting points, make good progress throughout the school and standards in RE are high. Teachers have secure subject knowledge supported by dedicated topic launch sessions for each new topic and have, and communicate, high expectations to the children.
Governors monitor the effectiveness of how Religious Education is taught in the school and use this information to inform future developments in the school’s provision.
Collective worship is central to the life of the school and children behave responsibly and with reverence during school and class Masses and other liturgical celebrations. There is a daily 15 minute collective worship session on every class timetable in addition to class prayers and assemblies. The children are very keen to participate in these sessions and be part of collective worship groups – there is currently a waiting list of children who would like to join the Mini Vinnies group. All of our staff participate in collective worship.

pageCache.pageTitle: Gospel Values – St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
At St Winefride’s we live our lives according to the Gospel Values.
Faithfulness is fundamental to our community. It may be witnessed in our Collective Worship and in the way we treat each other.
Dignity underpins everything we do. Every child, staff member, parent/carer, volunteer or helper is treated the same. We celebrate the attributes and talents of all.
Humility is shown each time we pray, gather together, greet each other. Everyone is treated equally, no one is better than anyone else.
Truth and integrity is paramount at St Winefride’s, we pride ourselves on our honesty, facing challenges as part of our mission and always being available to speak to our community at all times.
Forgiveness is at the heart of our school. Everyone has the chance to redeem themselves and it is never too late to begin.
Tolerance is enshrined in our Mission Statement:
“We celebrate God’s love for everyone. We enjoy learning and growing together, in our caring and welcoming family.”
Service is exemplified by the way our school community rises to the challenge of helping others who may be less fortunate than ourselves. The ‘Reverse Advent Calendar’ organised by our Mini Vinnies is a prime example of that.
Respect is always our starting point for any decision, plan or lesson. We care for all our community, leaving no one out, which we show to others by signing the ‘No Bystanders’ pledge every new school year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship – St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship is an integral part of life at St Winefride’s.
From our morning prayer onwards the children delight in worshipping Our Lord throughout the day. Collective worship has its own place in the curriculum but is also spontaneous.
The RE Team takes a lead in promoting collective worship and they help other children to learn the important prayers that will follow them throughout their lives.
We also take part in collective worship outside of school, every year we take a central role in the Remembrance Service at Central Park, East Ham, where we join all of the Catholic schools in the deanery, as well as several schools from the borough to remember the sacrifice of others that has enabled us to live free and safe lives.
The First Holy Communion programme is a very important way of combining school and church life, with the school helping to prepare the children for this most important sacrament, with the families joining together to celebrate this milestone in their children’s faith.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Life – St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
As a Catholic primary school, St Winefride’s aims to promote Gospel values in our work together and in our learning. The Catholic life of the school is rich in opportunities for children to encounter God and to deepen their relationship with Him as a loving, compassionate Father.
Through prayer, liturgies, Religious Education lessons and the relationships and support for each other that children, staff and parents/carers enjoy within the school community, we enable children to come to know and love God. This is brought together succinctly in our mission Statement:
“We celebrate God’s love for everyone. We enjoy learning and growing together, in our caring and welcoming family.”
Jesus said, “Let the children come to me.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Mass of Thanksgiving celebrating all school staff – St Winefride’s Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
On Tuesday 2nd September 2025 staff from all seven Our Lady of Grace Academy Trust schools came together for a Mass of thanksgiving at St Stephen’s Church Manor Park, celebrating all school staff and to mark the beginning of the new academic year.
The event was a lovely opportunity for teachers and support staff to join in prayer, reflect on their vocation and strengthen their shared commitment to serving students.
It was a beautiful and inspiring start to the year for everyone involved.
